kolam_txt: The kolam is a geometric prayer drawn on the ground with rice powder by Hindu women in front of the entrance of their homes during the festival of abundance.
During a month-long trip to India, I learned this ritual with a group of women from the art school “Sitaa” in Pondicherry.
That stay was a revelation for my rebuilding, as I was there to recover from a series of epileptic seizures, thanks to the help of my father and my stepmother.
I kept this kolam symbol. It is tattooed on my arm as a sign of divine protection and a tribute to creativity.
While composing the EP, I chose it as the logo of the RVL project. It seemed obvious to me that its feminine energy would support the intimate words and messages of my lyrics.
This feminine tradition is passed down exclusively from mother to daughter, for generations. Every morning at dawn, the women perform this ritual with the door of their house open.
It is a moment to honour their fertility and the creative nature of women, and then to protect their home for the year.
At sunrise, the rays passing over the drawing to enter the house are believed to fulfil the prayer of these women inside the home.
During this period, men walk around the drawing as they pass, to enter the house, as a sign of respect for the creative nature of Woman.
There are several standard models of kolam, and I chose the most ancestral one. It dates back to 300 BC.
It represents my music, through the universality of the themes explored around Woman.

ecriture.meta_description: Writing by Oriana Valenza: the book "Différente comme tout le monde" and "Ya Rashra", her mother's memoirs, currently being written.

oeuvres.image_alt: Cover of the book "Différente comme tout le monde": a woman with long hair and a red rose in her hair, black and white ink drawing
oeuvres.resume: Between poems, dances and existential questions, the journey of a little girl on the margins slaloms its way into adult life. She meets her experiences, not without a crash. Tinged with resilience and struggle, this story evokes dreams, illness, rape, travel and love. It stresses the importance of opening our eyes to the beauty of the World beyond obstacles. That little girl is you, it is me. We are all different, just like everyone.
Following recorded interviews with my mother, here are her memoirs. A life between North Africa and France. Lines that smell of jasmine!
